name: UPED
description: Underwater environment perception requires complementary optical, acoustic, and magnetic sensing modalities. Here, we present UPED, a high-resolution multimodal underwater dataset integrating RGB images, multibeam sonar images, laser point clouds, and triaxial magnetic measurements. The dataset was collected in a controlled seawater tank under three representative scenarios, including benthic biota, mineral enrichment, and subsea pipelines. UPED contains 2,400 RGB images, 2,400 sonar frames, 22 laser point-cloud sequences, and 2,600 magnetic samples. Among them, 2,000 low-overlap RGB images were manually annotated with 5,742 target instances. The dataset covers controlled variations in illumination, turbidity, temperature, and sound speed, while preserving synchronized multimodal measurements and sensor metadata. We further provide baseline experiments for object detection, underwater image enhancement, multimodal recognition, and simulation-to-real transfer. UPED provides a reproducible benchmark for developing and evaluating multimodal underwater perception methods.
